title: Eilmer of Malmesbury — the medieval monk who flew in the year 1010
voiceover: In the year 1010, almost 900 years before the Wright brothers, a Benedictine monk in England built a pair of wings, climbed to the top of a tower, and jumped. His name was Eilmer of Malmesbury. He glided for over 200 yards. Then he crashed, and broke both his legs. He survived. Bedridden, he was already planning his next attempt. He told friends he had failed because he didn't make a tail. His abbot, terrified, forbade him from ever trying again. He lived another 40 years, in a body that never walked right, dreaming of flight. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
